subject: ela
intro: Nonfiction books and articles use special text features to help readers find and understand information. Common text features include: subheadings (titles within a text that tell you what a section is about), bold print (important words made dark to stand out), captions (sentences under pictures that explain what the picture shows), glossaries (a list of hard words and their meanings at the back of a book), and indexes (an alphabetical list at the back of a book that tells you on which page to find specific information).

items.prompt: A nonfiction book about ocean animals has a section that begins with the words 'How Sharks Hunt' printed in large, dark letters. What text feature is this, and what does it tell the reader?

steps: The words are printed in large, dark letters at the beginning of a section.
This is a subheading — a smaller title that appears within the text.
A subheading tells the reader what that specific section is about.
This subheading tells the reader that the upcoming section will explain how sharks hunt.
solution.answer: This is a subheading. It tells the reader that the section will be about how sharks hunt. Subheadings help readers predict what they will learn and find specific information quickly.

items.prompt: In a science book about frogs, the word 'metamorphosis' is printed in bold. A sentence nearby says: 'Frogs go through metamorphosis, changing from tadpoles into adult frogs.' What text feature is bold print, and why do authors use it?

steps: Bold print makes text appear darker and heavier than the regular text.
Authors use bold print to signal that a word is especially important.
Bold words are often vocabulary words or key terms that readers should know.
In this case, 'metamorphosis' is bold because it is an important science word the reader should learn.
Bold print helps readers notice and remember key vocabulary.
solution.answer: Bold print is a text feature that makes important words stand out by printing them darker. Authors use it to show which words are key terms or vocabulary. Here, 'metamorphosis' is bold because it is the most important vocabulary word in that section.

items.prompt: A book about animals has a photograph of a gray wolf with the following words printed underneath: 'A gray wolf howls to communicate with the rest of its pack.' What text feature is this, and what information does it provide?

steps: Words printed beneath a photograph or illustration are called a caption.
A caption explains or describes what is shown in the image.
This caption tells the reader two things: the animal in the photo is a gray wolf, and it is howling to communicate with its pack.
Captions help readers understand what they are looking at and connect the image to the text.
solution.answer: This is a caption. It tells the reader that the photograph shows a gray wolf howling to communicate with its pack. Captions explain what images show and add information that might not be in the main text.

items.prompt: You are reading a nonfiction book about weather and you want to find the meaning of the word 'hurricane.' You turn to the back of the book and find a list of science words arranged alphabetically, each followed by its definition. What text feature is this, and where would you look to find 'hurricane'?

steps: A list of science words with their definitions at the back of a book is called a glossary.
A glossary is organized alphabetically, like a mini dictionary.
To find 'hurricane,' I would look under the letter H in the glossary.
A glossary helps readers find the meanings of important or difficult words used in the text.
solution.answer: This is a glossary. To find 'hurricane,' you would turn to the back of the book, find the glossary, and look under the letter H. A glossary provides definitions of important words used in the book.

items.prompt: You want to find all the pages in a science book that talk about volcanoes. You turn to the very back of the book and find a long alphabetical list of topics with page numbers next to each. What text feature is this, and why is it useful?

steps: An alphabetical list of topics with page numbers at the back of a book is called an index.
An index is different from a glossary — it does not give definitions, only page numbers.
I would look under V for 'volcanoes' to find all the page numbers where that topic appears.
An index is useful because it helps readers quickly find every page where a specific topic is discussed.
solution.answer: This is an index. It tells you on which pages to find information about specific topics. To find volcanoes, you would look under V and note all the page numbers listed, which is faster than reading the whole book.

items.prompt: A book about space exploration has a large photo of an astronaut floating inside a spacecraft. Below the photo, the words 'Astronaut Mae Jemison was the first African American woman to travel in space, flying aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour in 1992' are printed. What text feature is this, and what facts does it add that you might not get from just looking at the photo?
items.hint: Think about what text feature appears below photographs in nonfiction books.

steps: Text printed below a photograph is a caption.
Just looking at the photo, you would see an astronaut floating — but not who it is or what the significance is.
The caption adds: the astronaut's name (Mae Jemison), her historic achievement (first African American woman in space), the spacecraft (Space Shuttle Endeavour), and the year (1992).
solution.answer: This is a caption. Looking at the photo alone, you would only see an astronaut. The caption adds important facts: her name, her historic achievement, the spacecraft, and the year.

items.prompt: You are reading a nonfiction article about the rainforest. It is divided into sections. One section is labeled 'Animals of the Forest Floor' and the next is labeled 'Animals of the Canopy.' What text feature are these labels, and how would they help you if you only wanted to read about animals in the canopy?
items.hint: What do you call the smaller titles inside a nonfiction text?

steps: These section labels are subheadings.
Subheadings tell the reader what each section of the text is about.
If I only wanted to read about canopy animals, I could skip straight to the section labeled 'Animals of the Canopy' without reading the rest.
solution.answer: These are subheadings. They help you find specific sections quickly. If you only wanted to read about canopy animals, you could use the subheading to jump directly to that section.

items.prompt: You are reading a nonfiction book about the human body. In a section about the heart, you see the word 'ventricle' printed in bold. Nearby, a sentence reads: 'The ventricle is one of the heart's pumping chambers.' Why is 'ventricle' in bold, and how should you use this feature when reading?
items.hint: What does bold print signal to a reader about a word?

steps: 'Ventricle' is in bold because it is a key vocabulary word — an important term for understanding the heart.
Bold print is a signal: this word is important and I should pay close attention to it.
When reading, I should stop and make sure I understand the meaning of a bold word.
I might also look it up in the glossary if I need more explanation.
solution.answer: 'Ventricle' is in bold because it is a key science term. Bold print signals that a word is important vocabulary. When reading, you should pause and make sure you understand any bolded word, and check the glossary if needed.

items.prompt: A student wants to find information about the Lewis and Clark expedition in a history book. She does not want to read the whole book. Should she use the glossary or the index? Explain why.
items.hint: Think about what a glossary gives you versus what an index gives you.

steps: A glossary gives word definitions.
An index gives page numbers for topics.
The student wants to find where the Lewis and Clark expedition is discussed, not its definition.
She should use the index, look under L for 'Lewis and Clark,' and find the page numbers.
solution.answer: She should use the index. The glossary gives definitions of words, but the index tells you on which pages specific topics are discussed. She would look under L for 'Lewis and Clark' to find the relevant pages.

items.prompt: A nonfiction book about insects has the following text feature at the back: a list of words like 'antenna,' 'exoskeleton,' and 'larva,' each with a short definition. A student wants to know what 'larva' means. What should she do to find the answer?
items.hint: What text feature gives definitions of important words at the back of a book? How is it organized?

steps: A list of important words with definitions at the back of a book is a glossary.
A glossary is organized alphabetically.
The student should turn to the back of the book, find the glossary, and look under L for 'larva.'
solution.answer: The student should use the glossary at the back of the book. She should look under L for 'larva' to find its definition, since glossaries are organized alphabetically.
